source: United States federal rules for 2026 as amended in July 2025 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act), read from the IRS and from plan-provider summaries in summer 2026.
confidenceNote: The dollar limits are indexed and the law moves. Confirm each figure with the plan or a preparer before acting on it; the planner shows them so a family knows the question exists.

k12From529.label: 529 withdrawals for K to 12 tuition, per child per year
k12From529.note: Raised from ten thousand for 2026. Many states give a deduction on the way in; some claw it back on a K to 12 withdrawal. Check your state.

dependentCareFsa.label: Dependent care FSA, per household per year
dependentCareFsa.note: Raised from five thousand for 2026. Pays nursery, pre-K and day camp for a child under thirteen with pre-tax dollars, when both parents work.

childTaxCredit.label: Child tax credit, per child
childTaxCredit.note: Per child under seventeen, phasing out at higher incomes.

emergencyMonths.label: Emergency fund, months of the lean month
emergencyMonths.note: A family with tuition due every month wants the higher end of the usual three to six.

lifeCoverMultiple.label: Term life cover, multiple of income
lifeCoverMultiple.note: A large family with tuition ahead of it needs more years of income replaced than the usual ten. Term is cheap; both parents need it, including the one who earns less.

halachicWill.label: A will with a halachic clause
halachicWill.note: Torah inheritance rules and state law differ. A will that adds a shtar chatzi zachar, or a rabbinically drafted clause, lets both hold at once. Ask your rav and a lawyer who has done one.

heterIska.label: Heter iska
heterIska.note: A loan between Jews with interest needs a heter iska. Most Jewish-owned lenders and gemachs have one; ask before a private loan.
